content.text: A verified ten-case batch scored **0.7838**, closed **10/10 deals**, and reduced simulated total contract cost by **€1.189 million** versus opening offers. The agentic batches reviewed scored around **0.78** too, so the evidence supports stronger capabilities without yet proving that adding agents improved the average score.

**Codacabana is an autonomous procurement buyer that researches suppliers, negotiates by email, and evaluates the full economic value of a contract before accepting it.** The strongest pitch story is: **we evolved from scripted negotiation and regex-based interpretation into an agentic procurement team, while keeping financial decisions under deterministic control.** The logs show substantial progress, although they do not yet establish that adding agents outperforms the mature rules engine. **What the project does** Built for Hollerau Pumpenwerke in the Tacto Negotiation Arena, the buyer: - Studies supplier profiles, contracts, purchase history, forecasts, quality records, and cost indices. - Negotiates prices alongside payment, delivery, volume, duration, quality, and indexation. - Coordinates competing suppliers and uses their actual offers as negotiation evidence. - Accepts a valid standing offer when its total cost beats the alternative, or walks away. The company dataset contains **447 suppliers, 46 detailed supplier profiles, and 60 parts**. The business problem is that a cheaper unit price can still produce a more expensive contract through quality failures, financing, uncovered demand, or supplier relationship costs. **The evolution, supported by the logs** | Stage | What changed | Recorded result | |---|---|---| | **1. Scripted exploration** | Fixed sequences tested anchors, questions, term changes, and evidence. These runs helped reveal supplier behavior. | Initial export: **15 practice sessions, 0.2465 mean score**, 14 deals. This includes repeated cases and some manually resumed exploration. | | **2. Rules and regex engine** | Supplier traits and requests were recognized through text patterns. Code selected packages, prices, concessions, and closing actions. An optional LLM wrote an email paragraph. | Complete `practice-v5` batch: **0.7033**, **10/10 deals**. | | **3. Better economics and evidence** | Added clause trades, falling-index arguments, relationship-aware pricing, preservation of quoted packages, and closing fixes. | A later complete ten-case validation: **0.7838**, **10/10 deals**. | | **4. Agentic research and negotiation** | Added specialist researchers, strategy synthesis, simulated buyer/supplier rehearsal, and a live analyst that interprets replies and advises tactics. | Documented team batch: **0.7772**, **10/10 deals**. A context experiment scored **0.7604**, also 10/10. | | **5. Agentic refinement** | Tested richer session evidence and repaired proposal-generation failures. | Repaired candidate: **0.7808**, **10/10 valid deals**. Its report records **not promoted**. | Sources: [initial exports](https://github.com/stegra05/ehl-codacabana-final/blob/0fef4eebd26779f89cae02ce0bcf5b29fc2e157d/exports/README.md), [v5 log](https://github.com/stegra05/ehl-codacabana-final/blob/0fef4eebd26779f89cae02ce0bcf5b29fc2e157d/logs/practice-v5.log), [validation results](/Users/joaofmzuffo/ehl-codacabana-final/out/pr18-hosted-practice/20261010-225933/results.json), [team results](https://github.com/stegra05/ehl-codacabana-final/blob/0fef4eebd26779f89cae02ce0bcf5b29fc2e157d/docs/learnings.md), [repaired candidate](/Users/joaofmzuffo/ehl-codacabana-final/out/session-evidence-practice/20261011-064407/final-report.json). For the results slide, use **“0.70 → 0.78 across complete ten-case validations.”** Show the initial exploration separately because its case mix differs. The repository’s shorthand “0.32 → 0.66 → 0.73” lacks sufficiently clear batch definitions for a clean comparison. A useful engineering lesson: an earlier agentic evidence run scored **0.5257 with 7/10 deals**, following zero-price API errors and timeouts. Also, two evidence experiments averaged **0.7808 versus the preceding 0.7838 baseline**, so they were not promoted. Progress came through testing and rejecting regressions. **The business result to put on the slide** The **0.7838 ten-case validation** produced: | Metric | Result | |---|---:| | Deals closed | **10/10** | | Opening total contract cost | **€12.760 million** | | Negotiated total contract cost | **€11.571 million** | | Reduction versus opening offers | **€1.189 million / 9.32%** | These are **simulated contract economics across the benchmark case horizons**, not realized customer savings. An Arena score of 0.7838 is a normalized benchmark score, not a 78.38% price reduction. [Calculation evidence](/Users/joaofmzuffo/ehl-codacabana-final/out/pitch-evidence/summary.json). **The architecture today** ```mermaid flowchart TD D["Company data
Contracts, orders, forecasts, indices, supplier records"] R["Four research specialists
Economics · Persona · History · Leverage"] L["Lead researcher
Trade ideas, evidence priorities, tone"] H["Buyer and supplier rehearsal
Expected arguments and responses"] S["Supplier email and structured offer"] A["Live analyst
Requests, mood, argument, tactic"] P["Negotiation policy and supplier state"] E["Economic engine
Total cost, allowed terms, must-haves"] W["Writer
Approved figures, cited evidence, model paragraph"] O["Runner and Arena API
Scheduling, deadlines, send and recovery"] C["Closing gate
Valid standing offer below alternative cost"] M["Practice logs and memory"] D --> R --> L --> H --> P S --> A --> P P <--> E P --> W --> O --> S P --> C --> O O --> M M --> L ``` The responsibilities are deliberately separated: - **Research team:** four specialist model roles study different evidence; a lead researcher proposes trades and argument priorities. - **Rehearsal:** supplier and buyer roles anticipate objections and prepare responses. This is a planning simulation. - **Live analyst:** interprets each reply and selects constrained advice such as `steady`, `hold`, or `argue`. That advice can affect concession pacing and wording. - **Policy and economics:** calculate prices, value full packages using `arena_kit.total_cost`, validate constraints, and decide whether to accept. - **Writer:** combines exact code-selected terms and cited claims with model-written prose. - **Runner:** manages supplier clocks, parallel cases, API recovery, and closing before deadlines. - **Memory:** records practice outcomes for later preparation. The final runner disables new lesson recording. **Regex remains in the system**, particularly for supplier traits and request detection. The evolution is an agentic layer around an established economic engine, rather than a complete replacement. I checked this against `main` at **`0fef4ee`**. The architecture document still describes the earlier paragraph-only model role; the current [research](https://github.com/stegra05/ehl-codacabana-final/blob/0fef4eebd26779f89cae02ce0bcf5b29fc2e157d/buyer/research.py), [analyst](https://github.com/stegra05/ehl-codacabana-final/blob/0fef4eebd26779f89cae02ce0bcf5b29fc2e157d/buyer/analyst.py), and [policy](https://github.com/stegra05/ehl-codacabana-final/blob/0fef4eebd26779f89cae02ce0bcf5b29fc2e157d/buyer/policy.py) code establish the newer architecture. **Suggested pitch narrative** > “Procurement decisions depend on much more than price. Our buyer brings together supplier research, contract economics, and autonomous negotiation. > > We started with scripted experiments and regex rules to understand the environment. We then built an economic engine that evaluates complete contracts. Finally, we added a team of research and negotiation agents that interprets supplier context and adapts its arguments. > > In one complete ten-case validation, we closed every deal and reduced simulated total contract cost by €1.19 million, or 9.3%, versus opening offers. Our design gives language models room to interpret and negotiate while code controls the financial commitments.” Build the presentation around five slides: **problem → autonomous workflow → architecture → measured evolution → one negotiation example**. The refreshed practice catalog contains **468 completed sessions and 440 deals across all historical policies**. Use that as evidence of experimentation, not as the success rate of the current version. No final results were accessed.
